result.title: UI Best Practices: UI Best Practices
UX Best Practices for Digital Products
result.summary: Modern UX practice centers on reducing cognitive load while accelerating task completion across digital products. Research-driven design decisions consistently outperform intuition-based ones on conversion, retention, and satisfaction metrics. Nielsen's heuristics, layered information architecture, and progressive disclosure remain the highest-leverage foundations for product teams shipping at speed.
key_principles: Match the user's mental model — design around expectations users already hold from prior experience
Visibility of system status prevents anxiety and abandoned flows during every state transition
Progressive disclosure keeps complexity manageable as task depth grows
Fitts's Law governs target sizing — bigger and closer targets win on accuracy and speed
Hick's Law bounds choice — fewer visible options accelerate decision time
Errors are first-class design material — design recovery paths, not just prevention
Consistency (internal and external) builds predictable trust and reduces learning cost
do_list: Run 5–8 user interviews before sketching any screen to anchor the problem space
Card-sort to validate taxonomy before committing to navigation or IA
Prototype-test with at least 5 users per iteration (Nielsen's diminishing returns curve)
Use empty states to teach the core action, not just apologize for missing data
Provide undo or confirmation for any destructive or irreversible action
Make the primary action visually dominant via size, color, contrast, and position
Show progress in any flow exceeding two steps or five seconds
Support full keyboard navigation and visible focus states for all interactive elements
dont_list: Don't hide primary navigation behind hamburger menus on desktop viewports
Don't rely on color alone to convey state, error, or selection — pair with icon or text
Don't ship features without validating user demand through research or analytics
Don't bury the primary call-to-action below the fold on landing pages
Don't reset form state when validation errors occur — preserve user input
Don't use placeholder text as a substitute for persistent labels
Don't auto-play audio or video without an explicit user gesture
Don't use modal dialogs for non-modal information — they interrupt flow and break back-button expectations

patterns.name: Progressive Disclosure
patterns.description: Reveal advanced options only when context warrants it, keeping the default surface minimal.
patterns.example: Gmail's 'Advanced settings' hidden behind a single click in the standard view
patterns.use_when: Feature breadth risks overwhelming new or infrequent users

patterns.name: Breadcrumb Navigation
patterns.description: Show hierarchical location with clickable ancestors, enabling lateral escape from deep paths.
patterns.example: Amazon's product category path above the listing title
patterns.use_when: Content depth exceeds three levels or users frequently arrive mid-hierarchy

patterns.name: Sticky Primary Action
patterns.description: Pin the conversion or next-step button during scroll so it remains reachable on long pages.
patterns.example: Stripe Checkout's persistent 'Pay' button on the right rail
patterns.use_when: Page length risks the CTA scrolling out of view before completion

patterns.name: Modal vs Inline Editing
patterns.description: Choose modal for focused multi-field tasks; inline for single-field, low-risk corrections.
patterns.example: Notion's inline text editing versus Google Docs' comment thread modal
patterns.use_when: Edit complexity ranges from a single word to many dependent fields

patterns.name: Empty State as Onboarding
patterns.description: Use first-visit empty screens to teach the core action with templates or sample data.
patterns.example: Notion's template gallery shown when a workspace has zero pages
patterns.use_when: The primary value requires user-generated content that is hard to imagine cold

patterns.name: Skeleton Screens
patterns.description: Render structural placeholders during data fetch to reduce perceived latency.
patterns.example: LinkedIn feed shimmer while posts load
patterns.use_when: Data fetches regularly exceed 200ms and content shape is predictable

patterns.name: Command Palette Navigation
patterns.description: Replace deep menu hierarchies with a searchable keyboard-driven launcher.
patterns.example: Linear's Cmd+K palette for jumping to any project, issue, or setting
patterns.use_when: Power users form a meaningful share of traffic and the action space is large

metrics.name: Task Success Rate
metrics.why: Direct measure of whether users can complete core flows without assistance

metrics.name: Time on Task
metrics.why: Efficiency indicator; useful only when paired with success to avoid gaming

metrics.name: System Usability Scale (SUS)
metrics.why: Standardized benchmark enabling comparison across products and releases

metrics.name: Error Rate per Task
metrics.why: Signals friction, unclear affordances, or learnability issues

metrics.name: Net Promoter Score (NPS)
metrics.why: Loyalty and satisfaction proxy that correlates with retention

metrics.name: First-Time Task Completion
metrics.why: Onboarding effectiveness and immediate product clarity

metrics.name: HEART Framework Signals
metrics.target: Happiness, Engagement, Adoption, Retention, Task success — defined per feature
metrics.why: Google's framework for tying UX metrics to business outcomes without single-number fallacy

examples.feature: Developer-first onboarding with inline interactive code samples
examples.takeaway: Progressive disclosure scales complexity with user readiness instead of front-loading jargon

examples.feature: Cmd+K command palette as primary navigation layer
examples.takeaway: Search-driven navigation replaces deep menus and dramatically shortens task time for power users

examples.feature: Block-based empty states with curated templates
examples.takeaway: Empty states double as onboarding, inspiration, and time-to-value accelerator
Immediate feedback loops and visible progress teach through behavior, not instruction

examples.feature: Sticky search and filter bar on long listing pages
examples.takeaway: Persistent controls on long-scroll pages keep conversion reachable and reduce drop-off

examples.feature: Pull request review with inline comments and suggested changes
examples.takeaway: Inline feedback reduces context switching and keeps review and revision tightly coupled

references.title: 10 Usability Heuristics for User Interface Design
Information Architecture for the World Wide Web
HEART: A Framework for Measuring UX

action_items: Audit your top three user flows against Nielsen's 10 heuristics within the next week
Run a five-user usability test on the highest-traffic screen before the next release
Card-sort your primary navigation with at least 15 participants to validate the taxonomy
Define one core metric per feature that maps to a user outcome, not a vanity number
Replace all placeholder-text-as-label patterns with persistent labels across every form
Add undo or explicit confirmation to every destructive action currently in the product
Instrument empty, loading, and error states for every primary flow and review them quarterly
Establish a quarterly research cadence of five interviews per major persona segment
